description: Check Group Builder page -- a specialized editor for creating and managing check groups that bundle multiple individual checks into reusable test suites. Check groups allow users to compose verification steps from existing checks, controlling execution order, parallelism, and failure behavior. When used in a workflow verification phase, a check group runs all its constituent checks as a single verification unit, simplifying workflow configuration and promoting consistent verification patterns.

groups.name: Check Group Library Management
groups.description: The left panel presents all saved check groups in a searchable list following the standard library builder layout. Users can browse existing groups, create new ones, and select a group to load into the editor. Each list item shows the group name, the number of checks it contains, and any tags. The list supports search filtering to help users find specific groups in large libraries. Creating a new group opens a blank editor with default settings (sequential execution, stop on failure).

assertions.description: Users see the Check Groups page title within the standard library builder layout, identifying this as the check group management interface
Users can create a new check group, which opens a blank editor ready for naming, configuring execution mode, and adding checks from the library
Users can search through saved check groups by name to quickly locate a specific group for editing

groups.name: Check Composition and Ordering
groups.description: The core function of the check group editor is composing a group from existing checks in the library. Users see a list of available checks they can add to the group, and a list of currently included checks showing their order. The check selector shows check names, types, and tool information so users can identify the right checks. Users can add and remove individual checks from the group, building up a verification suite that covers all necessary validation points.

assertions.description: Users can add individual checks from the library to the group, building up a comprehensive verification suite from reusable check components

target.label: Check group editor with check selector

assertions.description: Users can remove checks from the group that are no longer needed, refining the verification suite to include only relevant validations

target.label: Check group editor with remove capability

assertions.description: The check selector displays check names and type information so users can identify and select the correct checks for their verification needs
Users can save the check group configuration, making it available as a single verification unit in workflow builder step pickers

groups.name: Execution Configuration
groups.description: Check groups support configuring how their constituent checks are executed. Users can choose between sequential execution (checks run one after another) and parallel execution (checks run concurrently for faster verification). The stop-on-failure flag controls whether the group halts at the first failing check or continues to run all checks to collect complete results. These options let users balance between execution speed, early failure detection, and comprehensive reporting depending on their workflow needs.

assertions.description: Users can choose between sequential and parallel execution modes, controlling whether checks run one at a time or concurrently for faster verification
Users can enable or disable stop-on-failure behavior, choosing between halting at the first failing check for early detection or running all checks for comprehensive results
Users can set a descriptive name and optional description for the check group to identify its purpose when selecting it in workflow builders

target.label: Check group name and description fields

assertions.description: Users can add tags to check groups for organization and discovery across the library dashboard

states.name: Empty Library — No Check Groups Exist
states.description: The page loads with no saved check groups. The left panel list is empty and the right panel editor shows a placeholder state inviting the user to create their first check group.

transitions.name: Create new check group
transitions.description: User clicks the New button to begin creating a check group, populating the editor with a blank form and default settings (sequential execution, stop on failure)

states.name: Populated — Check Group List with Editor Idle
states.description: One or more saved check groups exist and are displayed in the left panel list with name, check count, and tags. No group is actively selected for editing. The search box is available for filtering.

transitions.name: Select a check group to edit
transitions.description: User clicks a check group in the list to load it into the right-panel editor for viewing or editing

transitions.name: Create new check group
transitions.description: User clicks the New button to clear the editor and start a blank check group form

transitions.name: Enter search query
transitions.description: User types in the search box to filter the check group list by name

states.name: Search Active — Filtering Check Group List
states.description: A search query has been entered in the search box and the left-panel list is filtered to show only check groups matching the query by name.

transitions.name: Clear search query
transitions.description: User clears the search input to return to the full unfiltered check group list

transitions.name: Select a filtered check group
transitions.description: User clicks a check group from the filtered search results to load it into the editor

states.name: Editing New — Creating a Check Group
states.description: The editor is active with a blank check group form. Users can set the group name, description, tags, execution mode (sequential/parallel), stop-on-failure flag, and add checks from the library. The Save button is available.

transitions.name: Save new check group
transitions.description: User clicks Save to persist the new check group to the library, transitioning to editing-existing with the newly saved group loaded

transitions.name: Cancel or select existing group
transitions.description: User clicks a different check group in the list, discarding the unsaved new group

states.name: Editing Existing — Modifying a Saved Check Group
states.description: A saved check group is loaded in the editor. All fields are populated: name, description, tags, execution mode, stop-on-failure flag, and the list of included checks. Both Save and remove-check capabilities are available.

transitions.name: Save changes
transitions.description: User clicks Save to persist modifications to the existing check group

transitions.name: Create new check group while editing
transitions.description: User clicks the New button to clear the editor and start a fresh check group form

transitions.name: Select a different check group
transitions.description: User clicks another check group in the list to switch to editing that group instead
